entities.summary: Winfield Scott Hancock was a major general in the United States Army and the Democratic nominee for President of the United States in 1880. He served with distinction in the Army for four decades, including service in the Mexican–American War and as a Union general in the American Civil War. Known to his Army as "Hancock the Superb", he was noted in particular for his personal leadership at the Battle of Gettysburg in 1863. His military service continued after the Civil War, as Hancock participated in the military Reconstruction of the South and the United States's western expansion and war with the Native Americans at the Western frontier.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a Union general in the American Civil War and later as a key figure in Reconstruction, Hancock's leadership at the Battle of Gettysburg and his role in shaping the post-war South had significant regional impact. His military service also contributed to the United States's western expansion.
